text:
elsa: FYI nightly eval flagged a clear drop after promptpack v57 landed — rerank AUC down ~6% on our intent set. link to diff: https://git.internal/redwood/promptpacks/commit/abc123 :warning:

matt: ugh. any obvious change in content or ordering?

elsa: looks like v57 flipped the few-shot example order for the >2-turn templates (we moved the positive example to last). tiny textual edits too (removed clarifying comma).

jordan: ordering can change conditioning. did the eval-bot run the per-template breakdown?

ciara: eval-bot pasted summary: 
```
EVAL-BOT REPORT: promptpack v56 -> v57 diff on nightly-intent-suite
- overall AUC: 0.912 -> 0.856 (-6.0%)
- templates impacted: 12 / 48 (notably 'clarify-followup' and 'implicit-intent')
- failure mode: rerank score inversion, more false positives on terse queries
- commit: abc123
```

matt: sounds like an ordering-sensitive prompt. could be amplified by model changes or caching. which model/version was used for the nightly?

elsa: nightly used rwd-open-2.1-int8 (quantized canary). same model was used in previous run.

jordan: int8 quant + example order change could interact (precision shift in logits -> different argmax in reranker). we should test v56 vs v57 with fp16 and int8.

ciara: I'll run targeted A/B: v56/v57 on rwd-open-2.1-fp16 and -int8, 10k samples, same seeds. ETA ~30m.

elsa: thanks. if int8 only shows regression, that points at quant sensitivity which we can patch with small prompt stability heuristics. if both show regression then prompt edit is the issue.

matt: can we also run a canary that reorders examples back but keeps textual edits? isolate ordering vs wording.

jordan: yep do three arms: (A) v56 baseline, (B) v57 as-committed, (C) v57 with example-order reverted.

ciara: kicked off. quick note: I added a label to the PR `regression-investigate` and pinged @eng-oncall in the PR thread.

(eval-bot): canary jobs started — job ids: 9876 (A), 9877 (B), 9878 (C). will post results when ready. :gear:

elsa: also can we block merging further promptpack changes until we either rebaseline or revert? current failing PR is linked in the original commit.

matt: propose temporary policy: any promptpack PR that reorders examples must include a forced local eval and a one-line justification in PR description. approve if CI passes.

jordan: +1. also add a quick checklist item for quant-sensitivity checks when model in matrix is quantized.

(eval-bot): quick results: 
- A (v56 fp16): AUC 0.913
- B (v57 fp16): AUC 0.909 (small diff)
- A (v56 int8): AUC 0.911
- B (v57 int8): AUC 0.853 (big drop)
- C (v57 order-reverted int8): AUC 0.907

ciara: tl;dr: regression only appears with int8 and is fixed by reverting example order. ordering + int8 interaction is culprit.

elsa: okay that pinpoints it. options: revert v57 in promptpack, or keep v57 but add ordering-stability wrapper (force canonical ordering for quantized runs). which do we prefer?

matt: revert now, open a follow-up PR that preserves the author's textual intent but migrates examples in a quant-stable way. we need to avoid shipping breaks across quantized customers.

jordan: I'll draft the follow-up PR with tests: add an automated perturbation test (shuffle few-shot orders and ensure no >1% AUC variance on int8).

ciara: revert PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/promptpacks/pull/542 (revert abc123). added test TODO in description.

elsa: thanks. can someone with write access approve the revert? it's blocking canaries.

matt: approving now. :thumbsup:

jordan: once revert merges I'll run a quick nightly backfill and mark the failing alert as resolved. also we should add a small note in the promptpack CONTRIBUTING.md about quant-sensitivity.

elsa: agree. thanks everyone. leaving follow-ups: jordan to add perturbation test, author to re-implement change with ordering-stability, ciara to run post-merge nightly. tagging @eval-bot to re-run full nightly after merge. :white_check_mark:

(eval-bot): full nightly re-run queued after merge. will post results.
